newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung to further cut 16-mega DRAMs.
newsitem.headline: Samsung to further cut 16-mega DRAMs.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, the flagship of South Korea's Samsung Group, said on Thursday it would further cut production of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMS), citing worsening profitability because of low prices.
"We will continue to cut production of memory chips until we have an optimal price," a company statement said.
But Samsung, the world's largest memory chip maker, said production cuts would not affect buyers with long-term DRAM contracts.
Samsung began reducing production of 16 megabit DRAMs from the fourth quarter of 1996 because of deteriorating profits.
"Prices for 16 mega DRAMs fell below production cost. So all chip producers in Japan, the United States and Korea must consider cutting production if prices continue falling," the statement said.

Samsung said it would use extra production capacity after cutting 16 megabit output to make other memory chips such as graphic memories, and non-memory chips, including application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs).

Earlier, the U.S. unit of LG Semicon said the company had decided to shift some manufacturing resources out of 16 megabit DRAM production, which could result "over a period of time" in reducing its 16-meg output.
